summary: John Herbert Harington was an Indologist and historian. He served as secretary at the Asiatic Society from around 1794 to 1798 and was a professor at Fort William College from around 1801 to 1808.

John J. Holder works in philosophy and Buddhist studies, having studied under Harry Krebs. He held a visiting research appointment at the University of Oxford and served as Associate Professor of Philosophy at St. Norbert College (attested 2006, 2018).

John J. Makransky works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, earning his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1990. He held faculty posts at Boston College, Rangjung Yeshe Institute, and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

John Jorgensen specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned an MA under Kenneth H. J. Gardiner at the Australian National University, where he later held posts, as well as at Griffith University and La Trobe University.

John Kieschnick is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies. He taught at the University of Bristol from around 2003 to 2011 and became the Robert H. N. Ho Family Foundation Professor of Buddhist Studies at Stanford University around 2011.
John Lockwood Kipling was a historian and archaeologist educated at Woodhouse Grove School. He served as Curator of the Lahore Museum from around 1875 to 1893.

John M. Koller is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Indology who studied at the East-West Center under Shri Krishna Saksena and Charles A. Moore. He served as a professor of philosophy at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute.

John M. Rosenfield was a scholar of archaeology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at SMU, the University of Iowa, UC Berkeley, and Harvard University. He served as a professor at Harvard University from around 1965 to 1991.

John Marshall was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Dulwich College, King's College, and the University of Cambridge, he served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India from 1902 to 1931.
John Marston is a scholar in religious and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from the University of Washington in 1997. He held a post at El Colegio de México.

John Muir was an Indologist who studied at East India Company College and the University of Bonn. He served in the Bengal Civil Service from 1828 to 1853 and later held a post at the University of Edinburgh.
John Myrdhin Reynolds is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Dudjom Rinpoche (~1968–1987) and Namkhai Norbu (~1979–2018).

John Nemec is an Indologist, philosopher, and religious studies scholar educated at Rochester, UCSB, Oxford, and Penn (PhD 2005), studying under Alexis Sanderson. He was attested as Associate Professor of Indian Religions and South Asian Studies at the University of Virginia in 2020.
John Okell was a linguist educated at The Queen's College from around 1953 to 1957. He held a post at SOAS University of London from around 1959 to 1999.

John P. Keenan is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He held posts at the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture and Middlebury College.
John Peile was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. Educated at St. Bees School, Repton School, and Christ's College, Cambridge, he also studied under Theodor Benfey from around 1869 to 1870.
John Pickford was an Indologist who studied under Monier Monier-Williams. He served as a professor at the University of Madras.

John Powers is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who completed his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia. He held professorships at the Australian National University and Deakin University, and held a post at the University of Melbourne in 2022.
John R. B. Campbell is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisors Robert A. F. Thurman and Gary A. Tubb.

John R. McRae was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his Ph.D. at Yale under Stanley Weinstein. He held faculty posts at Cornell, Indiana University, Komazawa University, and Soka University.
